item.description: A swift and agile plant-eater from the Late Jurassic with powerful legs built for speed and five-fingered hands perfect for grasping vegetation.

item.title: Homotherium
item.description: Meet the scimitar cat Homotherium, a successful saber-toothed predator that roamed across continents for millions of years with its distinctive curved teeth and hyena-like build.

item.title: Megacerops
item.description: Adopt the mighty “thunder beast” that roamed North America with massive twin horns and a rhino-like build during the Cenozoic Era.

item.title: Synthetoceras
item.description: The largest protoceratid with an extraordinary Y-shaped forked horn on its snout that males used for territorial battles during the Miocene epoch.

item.title: Wolverine
item.description: The Wolverine is a fierce and powerful predator found in the forests and tundras of the Northern Hemisphere.

item.title: Whooping Crane
item.description: The whooping crane (Grus americana) is a strictly protected bird in North America. Once reduced to only 15 individuals in 1937, conservation efforts have increased their numbers to around 320 worldwide, including captive populations.
